# Ferralk

> Rust crates for finding files and matching globs, byte-first. `ferralk` walks a directory tree in parallel with root-relative include and exclude globs, optional `.gitignore` support, and pruning from the pattern itself. `ferralk-glob` compiles a glob once and matches it against paths or bytes you already hold; `ferralk` re-exports it as `ferralk::ferralk_glob`.

Pick the crate by what you hold. Files on disk: `ferralk::Walker`. A path or string in memory: `ferralk_glob::Pattern`, or `ferralk_glob::PatternSet` for a list of globs. Everything is synchronous; from async code, run a walk in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with a `CancellationToken` (recipe linked below).

**Matcher entry points.** Compile with `Pattern::compile(glob, PatternOptions::walker())?`, then pick how far a wildcard reaches. The pattern `*.rs` against three candidates:

| Candidate | `is_match` | `is_match_path` | `is_match_glob_path` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lib.rs` | yes | yes | yes |
| `src/lib.rs` | yes | yes | no |
| `./lib.rs` | no | yes | yes |

Use `is_match_glob_path` for paths: it reads a pattern as a shell and the walker do. `is_match` is for text in which `/` is not special. `is_match_path` and `filter_paths*` keep zlob's list rule, in which a wildcard in the first component crosses `/`.

**Two dialects.** `PatternOptions::default()` reads `**`, `{a,b}` and extglobs as plain text, so `src/**/*.rs` does not match `src/lib.rs` under it. `PatternOptions::walker()` turns all three on, exactly as `Walker` compiles its patterns. Add `.match_hidden(true)` for fast-glob's `dot: true` and `.case_insensitive(true)` for ASCII case folding; `Walker::case_insensitive(true)?` is the same folding for a walk.

**Walker defaults.** Each is off until asked for:

| Default | Change it with |
| --- | --- |
| `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, `.git/info/exclude` not read | `Walker::respect_git_ignore(true)`. The files in the walk root and below apply even outside a repository; inside one, `.git/info/exclude` and the files from the repository root down apply too. The global excludes file never does. |
| Files, directories and symlinks returned (never the root itself) | `WalkOptions::default().files_only(true)` |
| Include wildcards, `**` included, do not cover a leading `.`; hidden entries are still walked, and excludes cover them as `.gitignore` lines do | `Walker::match_hidden(true)` for includes; `WalkOptions::skip_hidden(true)` drops hidden entries |
| `*` stays inside one path component | `Walker::wildcard_mode(WildcardMode::SeparatorCrossing)` for the `globset` reading |
| Patterns match case-sensitively on every platform, even on a case-insensitive filesystem | `Walker::case_insensitive(true)?` folds ASCII case in includes, excludes and their pruning; the root of an absolute pattern and ignore files keep their own rule |
| Unsorted | `WalkOptions::sort(true)`, for `collect()` and `visit()` only; `Path` order, root included |
| Recoverable errors collected in `WalkResult::errors()` | `Walker::error_policy(ErrorPolicy::Abort)` to fail fast |
| Symlinks below the root not followed | `WalkOptions::follow_symlinks(true)` |

**Traps that compile and return the wrong result:**

1. `collect()?` returns `Ok` even when the root does not exist or a directory could not be read. Check `result.errors()`, or iterate the result: `for item in result` yields entries as `Ok`, then errors as `Err`. Branch on `error.operation()` and `error.io_kind()`, not the message. `ErrorPolicy::Skip` discards errors below the root; the default `Collect` keeps them.
2. Walker patterns are anchored at the root, unlike a slash-free `.gitignore` line: `exclude("target/**")` prunes only the top-level `target`. Write `**/target/**` for every depth.
3. `*` never crosses `/` in the walker or `is_match_glob_path`, unlike `globset`: `*.rs` selects top-level files only; write `**/*.rs`.
4. `**` is recursive only as a whole path component (`**`, `**/x`, `x/**`, `x/**/y`): `**/x` matches `x` and `a/x`, never `sx`. Elsewhere, as in `a**`, it is an ordinary star run.
5. A leading `!` is not negation. `Walker::include` and `exclude` reject it and `Pattern::compile` reads a literal `!`. Split a fast-glob or globby list: entries with `!` go to `exclude()` without it, except `!(…)`, which is a negated extglob.
6. `Walker::options(WalkOptions)` replaces every option; build one `WalkOptions` value and pass it once.
7. `stream()` ignores `sort(true)`, and `take(n)` counts `Err` items: use `.filter_map(Result::ok).take(n)` or handle errors first.
8. Returned paths include the root: `Walker::new(".")` yields `./src/lib.rs`. `entry.relative_path()` is `src/lib.rs`, the spelling the patterns matched; `WalkEntry::path_bytes()` also includes the root.
9. Patterns use `/` and `\` escapes on every platform, Windows included. Never build a pattern with `PathBuf::join`; keep the root in `Walker::new(root)`. To put a path or user text into a pattern literally, use `ferralk_glob::escape_str` (or `escape` for bytes); on Windows replace `\` with `/` first.
10. Patterns and candidates are bytes. For a `Path`, pass `ferralk_glob::path_bytes(path)`; a `&str` works as it is.
11. An include's `**` does not enter hidden directories: `include("**/*.ts")` misses `.cache/x.ts` until `match_hidden(true)`. Excludes are the opposite and cover hidden names as `.gitignore` lines do, even against an include that names one literally: `include(".github/**")` with `exclude("**/*.yml")` drops `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
12. For a list of globs use `ferralk_glob::PatternSet`, the `globset::GlobSet` counterpart: `PatternSet::new(globs, PatternOptions::walker())?`, then `is_match_glob_path(path)` or `matches_glob_path_into(path, &mut indices)`. Its methods read patterns like the `Pattern` entry point of the same name, so `PatternSet::is_match` crosses `/`; a looped `Vec<Pattern>` answers the same, only slower.
13. `Verdict::Skip` from `visit()` drops an entry but still walks a directory's subtree; `Verdict::Prune` drops it and does not walk below it.

## Recipes

- [ferralk recipes](https://docs.rs/ferralk/latest/ferralk/#recipes): tested examples for listing files with `.gitignore`, include and exclude lists from a fast-glob style list, stopping early, continuing past errors, cancelling from another thread, and async use with `spawn_blocking`.
- [ferralk-glob recipes](https://docs.rs/ferralk-glob/latest/ferralk_glob/#recipes): matching one path against several globs, porting a fast-glob `!` list, matching a `Path`, putting literal text into a pattern, filtering lists, reporting an invalid pattern at its offset.
- [Examples](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/tree/main/crates/ferralk/examples): one program per recipe, run as `cargo run -p ferralk --example <gitignore_walk|include_exclude|early_stop|keep_going> -- <root>`.
- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/skills/ferralk/SKILL.md): this guidance as a loadable skill for coding agents.

## Docs

- [Usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/docs/usage.md): every walker default and the switch that changes it, the matcher entry points and options, errors, cancellation, hidden files.
- [Compatibility guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/docs/compatibility-guide.md): a migration table from `globset`, `glob`, fast-glob and globby, `ignore`, and `walkdir`, then the mapping from zlob 1.6.3.
- [Consumer pattern contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/docs/consumer-contract.md): for a program that passes its users' globs on: what 1.x covers per dialect and entry point, validating with `Walker::try_include`, escaping literal text with `ferralk_glob::escape`, which error fields are stable, and porting from `globset`.
- [ferralk API](https://docs.rs/ferralk): `Walker`, `WalkOptions`, `WalkResult`, `WalkEntry`, `WalkError`, `ErrorPolicy`, `CancellationToken`.
- [ferralk-glob API](https://docs.rs/ferralk-glob): `Pattern`, `PatternSet`, `PatternOptions`, `PatternError`, `PatternSetError`, `escape`.

## Optional

- [1.x stability contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/docs/stability.md): what 1.x promises and what it excludes.
- [Public API listings](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/tree/main/docs/api): every public item of both crates, as `cargo public-api` prints it.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sebastian-software/ferralk/main/README.md): positioning, comparison with other crates, and benchmarks.
